role: WindowSelector configuration and selection logic: 30-70% sleep band resolution on the series' t_ms timeline (wall-clock to t_ms translation), two-pass artifact scanning (the 15% pass when the strict pass has no organized window, or no window for peak search), organized-window ranking (Tier 1 score or RMSSD), peak-capacity scan, peak-metric and manual window selection, zone merging, adaptive window sizing.
types: WindowSelector.Config: struct — window size 400, step 40, artifact limits 0.10/0.15, minCleanBeats 300, band 0.30-0.70, stabilityWeight 10, isolatedSpikeRatio 1.5 (the ectopic gate is TimeDomainAnalyzer's)
WindowSelector.SleepBoundaries: struct — recording and sleep boundaries as t_ms positions (plus durations)
WindowSelector.SearchBand: struct — index range and ms limits of the band
toplevel: Config property defaults (S:12-70) set every selector threshold; Config.default = Config().

units.does: Main automatic selector: clears lastOrganizedZones, resolves the 30-70% sleep band (searchBand, verbose), scans it with the strict 10% artifact pass and falls back to the permissive 15% pass when the strict pass yields no ORGANIZED window, and returns the best organized window (Tier 1 ranked with a baseline, else RMSSD) or nil; populates lastOrganizedZones as a side effect.

branches.cond: searchBand returns nil (<120 beats, no points, or empty band)
no windows survive either artifact pass
branches.effect: return nil; else select organized window

units.does: Requires >=120 beats, resolves sleep boundaries (t_ms positions), finds the 30-70% search band and returns (boundaries, band) or nil; with verbose (the organized search) it also logs the resolved boundaries and the band details. Shared by findBestWindow and findPeakMetricWindow; it does not touch lastOrganizedZones.

branches.effect: log 'No points' and return nil (unreachable after the 120-beat guard)
log the band; then return (boundaries, band)

units.does: Scans the band at the strict 10% artifact limit and returns those windows when they suffice: with requireOrganized (findBestWindow) when any is isOrganizedRecovery, else (findPeakMetricWindow) when any exists. Otherwise rescans at config.maxArtifactRate (15%), a superset of the strict windows, logs the fallback (or that none were found) and returns that scan (empty when it finds none).

branches.effect: strict suffices when it holds an organized window; else when it holds any window
return the strict windows; else rescan at 15%
log 'no valid windows even at 15%'; else log the fallback; return the permissive windows

units.does: Applies filterIsolatedSpikes to the windows and logs how many were rejected; returns the kept windows.

branches.effect: log rejection count; else nothing extra

units.does: Spike-filters the windows (never empty for a non-empty input: edge windows are never spikes), keeps only isOrganizedRecovery ones, stores their merged time ranges in lastOrganizedZones, and builds the recovery window from them; nil when none are organized.

branches.effect: log and return nil (peak fallback happens in caller); else buildRecoveryWindow

units.does: Writes the merged start/end ranges of the organized windows into lastOrganizedZones.

Logs the boundaries as resolveSleepBoundaries resolved them (after the wall-clock translation), in minutes into the recording: the sleep start or 'using recording start', the wake or why the recording end is used, and the recording/sleep spans.

branches.effect: log the resolved start minute; else log 'using recording start'

branches.cond: resolved sleep end before the recording end
branches.effect: log the resolved wake minute; else log that the wake was past the recording or not after sleep start and the recording end is used

units.does: Logs the band limits (minutes into the recording), band duration/beats and adaptive window size for diagnostics.
Scans the band with the adaptive window/step size using sleep start/end as the relative-position span and the given artifact limit.
Ranks organized windows (Tier 1 score vs baseline when baselineStats given, else RMSSD) and builds the RecoveryWindow from the top one; nil for an empty list.

branches.effect: rank by Tier 1 score; nil baseline uses rankByRMSSD
return nil; else build from first

units.does: Scores each organized window with RecoveryScoreCalculator.calculateTier1 (rmssd, meanHR, a1, baseline, no readiness), logs the ranking, and sorts by score, then RMSSD, then later relative position.

branches.effect: higher RMSSD first; else later relativePosition first

units.does: Logs one multi-line ranking entry: each organized window's rank, relative position and start minute, with its Tier 1 score and metrics redacted (as logSelectedWindow redacts them) because the log is user-exportable.
Sorts organized windows by RMSSD descending, ties to later relative position, and logs the no-baseline fallback.

branches.effect: higher first; else later position first

units.does: Builds the RecoveryWindow from the chosen organized block: isConsolidated = HR CV < 0.08 (always true in production, where an organized block without LF/HF is HR-stable; false only for a test block organized by LF/HF), qualityScore = RMSSD/100, recoveryScore with stability weight, isOrganizedRecovery true, classification from the block.
Formats the stored selection reason 'Organized Recovery (RMSSD x ms, a1=y, CV z%) at p%'.
Logs the selected window (values redacted), warning when its position lies outside the configured band.

branches.effect: log warning with timestamps; else no warning

units.does: Sorts time ranges by start and merges ranges that overlap or touch into contiguous zones.

branches.effect: extend the last merged zone; else append as new zone

units.does: Combined entry used by the analysis pipeline: requires >= beatsPerWindow (400) beats, gets an organized recovery window or the peak-RMSSD fallback, computes peak capacity across the whole recording, and returns both (nil only when neither exists).

branches.effect: return nil if recovery window also nil, else result with peakCapacity nil

flags.text: baselineStats defaults to nil, so callers that omit it silently switch ranking from Tier 1 score to raw RMSSD; RRCollector+DeviceRecording:186 omits it while HRVAnalysisPipeline/SessionRecoveryService/ReanalysisService pass one, so device-recording results can pick a different window than morning processing for the same night (ReanalysisService:210 documents this exact divergence as a past bug).

units.does: Returns findBestWindow's organized window when there is one, else the peak-RMSSD window in the same band.

branches.effect: log and return it; else fall back to peakRMSSDFallback

units.does: Runs findPeakMetricWindow(.rmssd) in the 30-70% band and logs whether a window was found.

branches.effect: log success; else log 'will analyze full session'

units.does: Scans the entire recording with the compact adaptive window, spike-filters, and returns PeakCapacity from the highest-RMSSD sustained window (relative position against recording span); nil for an empty series or no windows.
Maps the peak block to PeakCapacity (RMSSD, SDNN, totalPower nil, duration minutes, relative position, mean HR).
Logs the peak-capacity scan's recording length, beat count, BPM and window size.
Dispatches by WindowSelectionMethod: consolidatedRecovery → findBestWindow (no baseline), peak methods → findPeakMetricWindow with the metric, custom → nil.

branches.effect: findBestWindow without baselineStats (RMSSD ranking; production reaches Tier 1 ranking through findBestWindowWithCapacity instead)
findPeakMetricWindow(.totalPower), ranked by SDNN as the total-power proxy

units.does: Selects the window with the highest RMSSD or SDNN (also for total power) in the 30-70% band — searchBand without verbose logging, the strict-then-permissive artifact passes falling back only when the strict pass finds no window, then the spike filter — regardless of organization, and builds a RecoveryWindow.

branches.effect: log and return nil (unreachable: the spike-filtered set of a non-empty input is non-empty); else build window

units.does: Logs the peak-selection band duration, beats and adaptive window size.
Returns the candidate with max RMSSD for .rmssd, else max SDNN (logging that total power is approximated by SDNN).
Builds a RecoveryWindow for a peak-selected block, carrying its real isOrganizedRecovery and isConsolidated = organized && CV < 0.08.
Formats 'Peak <metric> (value ms, a1, CV%) at p%' and logs the selection.
Returns the metric name and formatted value: RMSSD, SDNN, or 'SDNN (Total Power proxy)' with the SDNN value.

User 'Pick Window' path: requires >=400 beats, centres a 400-beat window on the beat closest to targetMs (a tap before the first or past the last beat lands on it; pulled back at recording end), evaluates it with the artifact gate disabled (limit 1.0) and returns the manual RecoveryWindow; nil when too short or too little signal.

branches.effect: return nil; else build manual window

flags.text: No test calls analyzeAtPosition, the user-facing manual window override.

units.does: Centres a beatsPerWindow window on the beat closest to targetMs (closestBeatIndex) and shifts it back to fit when it would overrun the end; always returns indices (points is non-empty).

branches.effect: clamp end to count and start to max(0, end-400); else keep centred window

units.does: Index of the beat whose t_ms is nearest targetMs: the first beat at or after it, or the one before when that is strictly nearer; the last beat when targetMs is past the end; 0 when it is before the first beat.

branches.cond: the match is the first beat

units.does: Evaluates the manual window with artifactRateLimit 1.0 so only the >=50 valid RR and clean-beat guards can reject it; logs and returns nil on rejection.

branches.effect: log 'too little usable signal' and return nil; else return block

units.does: Builds the manual RecoveryWindow carrying the block's isOrganizedRecovery and isConsolidated = organized && CV < 0.08.
Formats 'Manual selection at p% (RMSSD, a1, CV%)'.
actualSleepEndMs - actualSleepStartMs.
Whole minutes from the first beat (recordingStartMs) to the given t_ms position, for log lines.
endExclusive - startIdx.

Resolves every boundary as a position on the series' own t_ms timeline: recording start/end = first/last t_ms; sleep start = the t_ms of the first beat received at/after the wall-clock sleep start (tMsPosition), floored at the recording start (recording start when absent); sleep end from the wake via sleepEnd. findSearchBand and the window relative position then compare like with like whatever the first beat's t_ms is.

branches.effect: sleep start = recording start; else max(recording start, translated position)

units.does: The wake's t_ms position (tMsPosition) clamped to the recording end when it lies after the sleep start; otherwise the recording end.

branches.effect: return min(wake, recording end); else recordingEndMs

units.does: Maps a wall-clock offset from session start onto the t_ms timeline: the t_ms of the first beat whose wallClockMs (ms since the stream/session started, the same clock as the offset) is >= the offset, skipping beats without a wall clock; the last beat's t_ms when none is; the offset itself when the series carries no wall clock (H10 internal, whose t_ms counts from session start).

branches.cond: no points, or the first point has no wallClockMs
branches.effect: return the offset unchanged (H10 internal path)

branches.cond: a beat with wallClockMs >= offset exists

units.does: Computes the 30%-70% points of the sleep span (t_ms positions), clamps them to the recording's first/last t_ms, and returns the index range of beats inside, or nil when empty.

branches.cond: a start index and end index exist with end >= start

units.does: Window size: beatsPerWindow when enough beats; otherwise half (band) or a third (compact) of the beats when >= 240/360 beats, else max(60, 60%/40%); step = max(10, size/10).

branches.effect: beats/3 if >= 360 else max(60, 2/5 of beats)
